---
title: Model presets
description: "Architecture and fit presets derived from the frozen arena HPO recipes, with explicit local overrides."
engine: markdown
---

Use `rf.Model(preset="small", ...)` to build a schema with named architecture
defaults. Use `model.fit(data, preset="small")` to select training defaults
independently. Each constructor creates a fresh, untrained model; a fit preset
starts a new optimizer run unless `ckpt_path` resumes an existing one.

## Bundled architectures

The `small` and `medium` presets extract the architecture from the frozen
`Desktop/arena` research recipes `small-regularized-capacity` (SMALL trial 33)
and `medium-deep-context` (MEDIUM trial 8). The latter was also used for the
large-task panel. Their source configurations and hashes are recorded in
`relflow/presets/provenance.json`.

These are data-regime names, not an ascending parameter-count ladder:

| Setting | `small` | `medium` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Shared width, `d_model` | 128 | 64 |
| Root encoder layers | 2 | 2 |
| Root encoder heads | 4 | 8 |
| Root feed-forward multiplier, `ffnx` | 2 | 4 |
| Child branch encoder layers | 1 | 2 |
| Child branch heads | 4 | 4 |
| Child branch `ffnx` | 8 | 8 |
| Child attention outputs | 4 | 1 |
| Leaf decoder heads | 4 | 4 |
| Leaf decoder `ffnx` | 8 | 8 |
| Leaf decoder blocks, `n_linear` | 1 | 1 |

Both use MHA, zero encoder and decoder dropout, query-pooled decoders,
and a root attention reduction with one output. Attention reductions have
one layer and positional information; their heads and dropout inherit their
owning branch. Leaf decoder positioning remains automatic: off for scalar
targets and on for repeated targets. Hidden activations use tanh GELU and
normalization uses RMSNorm.

The source recipes came from retrospective development-task calibration.
Extracting their architecture is not a new benchmark, a complete reproduction
of those experiments, or a general prediction-quality guarantee. Schema shape,
vocabularies, decoded fields, and external text encoders also determine model
size and cost.

## Declare fields and override the root

```python
import relflow as rf


class Transaction(rf.Branch):
    booked_at = rf.Period("day_of_month", "day_of_week", "hour_of_day")
    amount = rf.Number
    merchant = rf.Category
    disputed = rf.Boolean(mask=True, n_heads=2)


class PaymentModel(rf.Model):
    trxns = Transaction(length=32, overflow="tail", ffnx=4)


model = PaymentModel(preset="small", n_layers=3)
```

The constructor changes the root depth to three. The history keeps the
preset's branch depth of one and its explicit `ffnx=4`; its field decoders
keep their own `ffnx=8`. Only the dispute decoder changes its heads to two.
The same presets work with ordinary keyword fields and `fields={...}` mappings.

`d_model` is shared across the model. All other architecture defaults belong
to their own root, branch, or leaf. A width override must be compatible with
every effective attention head count; changing root heads does not rewrite
branch or leaf heads. Registered third-party tensorfields receive the common
leaf defaults while retaining their extension options.

## Omission and explicit values

At each node, an explicit option wins, an omitted option takes its scope's
preset default, and options outside the preset retain their ordinary defaults.

An explicit reduction replaces the whole reduction object. For example,
`reduction=rf.Attention()` selects one output, while `rf.Mean()` and `None`
replace the attention reduction completely. Explicit `attention=None` disables
encoder attention, and `dropout=None` selects zero dropout. Explicit
`decoder_position=None` keeps the automatic scalar/repeated-target policy.
Reusing a branch or leaf creates independent resolved definitions.

The architecture preset leaves collection lengths, overflow, queries, masking,
objective choices, jitter, data preparation, and runtime settings to the
application. It does not apply the source recipe's input or branch masking.
A child named `preset` belongs in a class declaration or a mapping:

```python
model = rf.Model(preset="small", fields={"preset": rf.Category})
```

Without a preset, `rf.Model(...)` still requires `d_model`, `n_layers`, and
`n_heads`. `preset=None` keeps that behavior.

## Fit presets

```python
model.fit(
    datamodule,
    preset="small",
    batch_size=128,
    learning_rate=1e-4,
)
```

The explicit batch size and learning rate replace the preset's values.
Constructor and fit selections are independent: a model built with `small`
can fit with `medium`, and constructing a model with a preset does not
implicitly select one for later fits.

| Fit setting | `small` | `medium` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Per-device batch size | 64 | 512 |
| AdamW learning rate | 0.0001504508367492947 | 0.00021681002964478338 |
| Weight decay | 0.01 | 0.0 |
| Epochs | 8 | 8 |
| EMA decay | 0.995 | 0.995 |
| Gradient norm clipping | 0.25 | 0.25 |
| Early stopping and rollback | Disabled | Disabled |

Eight epochs express the source recipes' eight-pass budget for an ordinary
finite loader. Loader sampling, batch limits, distributed sharding, and custom
loader behavior still determine the actual examples and updates. An explicit
`max_epochs`, `max_steps`, or `max_time` replaces the epoch default. Batch sizes
are defaults, not a resource guarantee or automatic OOM fallback.

An explicit optimizer replaces the preset's AdamW defaults. Use
`ema_decay=None` to disable averaging or supply your own `rf.EMA` callback to
replace its default. Explicit stopping and rollback options also win. Fit
presets leave the architecture, schema masks, jitter, collection policy,
hardware, and input splits unchanged. See [Training options](../guides/training-options.qmd).

## Custom policies

Register an immutable policy under a unique name:

```python
compact = rf.presets.Preset(
    name="payment-compact",
    revision=1,
    d_model=96,
    root=rf.presets.BranchDefaults(
        n_layers=2,
        n_heads=4,
        reduction=rf.Attention(),
    ),
    branch=rf.presets.BranchDefaults(
        n_layers=1,
        n_heads=4,
        reduction=rf.Attention(n_outputs=2),
    ),
    leaf=rf.presets.LeafDefaults(n_heads=4),
    fit=rf.presets.FitDefaults(
        batch_size=128,
        learning_rate=1e-4,
        weight_decay=0.01,
        max_epochs=20,
        ema_decay=0.99,
    ),
)
rf.presets.register(compact)

model = PaymentModel(preset="payment-compact")
model.fit(datamodule, preset="payment-compact")
```

Registration validates and copies the policy. Names must be nonempty and
unique, including bundled names; revisions must be positive. The optional
`fit` configuration is required only when selecting that policy in `fit`.
Retrieve a policy with `rf.presets.get(name)`.

## Save, load, and extend

The resolved schema records the actual architecture, and `model.preset`
records its immutable construction policy. Checkpoints retain both; loading
does not look up the preset again or apply newer defaults. Extending a saved
model uses its saved policy only for the new nodes. Existing nodes retain
their resolved options. See [Schema mutation](../guides/schema-mutation.qmd).

`rf.Model(schema=schema)` restores a resolved architecture and cannot combine
it with `preset=...`. YAML templates select the same registered policies with
`preset: small`; see [Model templates](../guides/model-templates.qmd).

## Migrating to 0.5.0

The generated `.xs()` through `.xl()` methods, `rf.presets.factory`,
`.with_preset(...)`, the `XS`–`XL` constants, and the old size names are removed.
Choose `small` or `medium` and reevaluate it on your task: these are new
architectures, not renamed equivalents. Saved checkpoint schemas and policies
remain authoritative, including historical policies with retired names.
